modules.algo.may: Sorting, searching, grouping and eager list transformations.
modules.collections.may: List-backed stacks and queues and map-backed sets.
modules.csv.may: Quoted comma-separated text parsing, serialization and records.
modules.format.may: Text tables, percentages, durations, byte sizes and ANSI formatting.
modules.functional.may: Composition, currying, partial application and memoization.
modules.io.may: Text, line, JSON, CSV and key-value file helpers.
modules.iter.may: Eager list iteration, scans, windows and keyed reductions.
modules.math.may: Arithmetic, number theory and geometric helpers.
modules.native.may: Automatically available full-runtime helpers; a byte-identical mirror of the injected sidecar compiler/mayc/native.may.
modules.net.may: Synchronous IPv4 TCP/UDP sockets for full Linux x86-64 runtimes.
modules.path.may: Lexical path operations without filesystem access.
modules.prelude.may: Automatically loaded small convenience functions in full-runtime builds.
modules.stats.may: Descriptive statistics and simple linear regression.
modules.string.may: String transformations and simple delimiter helpers.
modules.test.may: Counting assertions and a final test report.
modules.validate.may: Input predicates and structured rule/field validation.
modules.core: Core-runtime additions to the shared library: raw allocation, typed scratch arenas, the retained heap size, gcd and lcm. The core runtime also loads prelude.may and native.may.
modules.ui.may: Native Linux desktop widget trees, themes, antialiased GPU shapes/text, layout, Unicode inputs, focus, scrolling, virtual lists and software PNG snapshots; requires the May UI Sokol adapter.

symbols.constantly: Return a unary function that always returns `value`.
symbols.flip: Return a binary function calling `f(b, a)`.
symbols.curry: Convert a binary function into two nested unary functions.
symbols.uncurry: Convert a curried function into one taking two arguments.
symbols.apply_n: Return the result of applying `f` to `x` `n` times; nonpositive counts leave `x` unchanged.
symbols.enumerate: Return `[index, value]` pairs in input order.
symbols.zip_with: Return `f(a[i], b[i])` for each pair, stopping at the shorter list.
symbols.find_index: Return the first index satisfying `pred`, or `-1`.
symbols.find_value: Return the first value satisfying `pred`, or `fallback`.
symbols.take_while: Return the longest initial prefix satisfying `pred`.
symbols.drop_while: Return the suffix after the initial prefix satisfying `pred`.
symbols.scan: Return `[seed, f(seed, x0), ...]`, including the initial accumulator.
symbols.windows: Return all overlapping consecutive windows of positive `width`; return `[]` when width exceeds length.
symbols.pairwise: Return overlapping adjacent value pairs; fewer than two inputs produce `[]`.
symbols.sum_by: Sum `f(x)` over inputs, starting at integer zero.
symbols.min_by: Return the element with the smallest `f(x)` score; `nil` for empty input; ties retain the earliest element.
symbols.max_by: Return the element with the largest `f(x)` score; `nil` for empty input; ties retain the earliest element.
symbols.cartesian: Return all `[x, y]` pairs, with `a` as the outer iteration.
symbols.stats_mean: Return the floating arithmetic mean, or `nil` for empty input.
symbols.stats_sum_squares: Return the sum of squared values, starting at `0.0`.
symbols.stats_variance: Return population variance (divide by `n`), or `nil` when empty.
symbols.stats_sample_variance: Return sample variance (divide by `n - 1`), or `nil` for fewer than two inputs.
symbols.stats_stddev: Return the square root of population variance, or `nil` when empty.
symbols.stats_zscores: Return standardized values using population deviation; empty/constant inputs produce zeros.
symbols.stats_quantile: Sort and linearly interpolate at `q * (n - 1)`; empty input returns `nil`; nonempty input requires `q` in `[0, 1]`.
symbols.stats_mode: Return a most frequent original value, or `nil`; counts use stringified keys.
symbols.stats_covariance: Return sample covariance of the common prefix, or `nil` for fewer than two pairs.
symbols.stats_correlation: Return covariance divided by the two sample deviations; return `nil` for insufficient/constant data. Use equal input lengths for consistent normalization.
symbols.stats_linear_regression: Return `{slope, intercept, r}` using the common prefix; require at least two points and varying x values.
symbols.csv_parse: Return rows of string cells; handle quoted commas/newlines, doubled quotes and CRLF; reject unterminated quotes; skip blank unquoted lines.
symbols.csv_escape: Stringify and quote empty cells or cells containing commas, quotes or line breaks; double embedded quotes.
symbols.csv_stringify: Serialize row lists with commas and LF between rows, without a final newline.
symbols.csv_records: Return a list of maps keyed by headers; short rows fill with empty strings and extra cells are ignored.
symbols.path_substr: Return characters from inclusive `start` to exclusive `stop` as a string.
symbols.path_is_absolute: Recognize leading `/` or a drive letter followed by `:/` or `:\`.
symbols.path_normalize: Replace backslashes with `/`, remove repeated separators and `.`, resolve lexical `..`, preserve roots; empty relative paths become `.`.
symbols.path_join: Join and normalize two paths; an absolute second path replaces the first.
symbols.path_basename: Return the final component after normalization; the root `/` yields an empty string.
symbols.path_dirname: Return the normalized parent path, preserving roots; a lone relative component has parent `.`.
symbols.path_extension: Return the extension without its dot; dotfiles and trailing dots produce an empty string.
symbols.path_stem: Return the basename without its final extension.
symbols.path_relative: Return a lexical relative path; equal paths produce `.` and mismatched roots raise a fault.
symbols.validate_nonempty: True for a string with non-whitespace content after trimming.
symbols.validate_in_range: True for an Int/Float within the inclusive bounds; false for other types.
symbols.validate_email: Apply a simple @/domain-dot heuristic; this is not a complete email parser.
symbols.validate_url: True for strings beginning with `http://` or `https://`.
symbols.validate_all: Apply rules shaped `{check: unary predicate, message: string}` and return `{ok, errors, value}`.
symbols.validate_required_fields: Return `{ok, missing}`; absent keys and nil-valued fields are missing.
symbols.validate_int_string: Check a nonempty string by attempting trimmed integer conversion and catching faults.
symbols.validate_float_string: Validate signed decimal syntax with optional dot and exponent; exponent digits are required.
symbols.format_percent: Return a ratio multiplied by 100, rounded through `round` and decorated with `%`; `digits` controls scale, not zero-padding.
symbols.format_bytes: Return bytes or binary KiB/MiB/GiB/TiB notation using 1024-based scaling.
symbols.format_duration: Clamp negative integer seconds to zero and return `MM:SS` or `HH:MM:SS`.
symbols.format_table: Return a pipe-delimited text table with widths from headers and rows; missing cells are empty and extra columns are ignored.
symbols.format_kv: Return newline-separated key/value lines with keys padded to `width`.
symbols.format_ansi: Wrap stringified text in an ANSI SGR code and reset sequence.
symbols.format_color: Wrap text with the supplied ANSI color code.
symbols.io_read_text: Read an entire text file; propagate read errors.
symbols.io_read_or: Read text or return `fallback` on a caught runtime fault.
symbols.io_write_text: Write `str(text)` and return the supplied path.
symbols.io_read_lines: Read a file and split on LF; a trailing newline yields a trailing empty entry.
symbols.io_write_lines: Join lines with LF, write without an added final newline, and return the path.
symbols.io_read_json: Read and parse JSON; propagate I/O and parse errors.
symbols.io_read_json_or: Read and parse JSON, returning `fallback` on any caught fault.
symbols.io_write_json: Serialize JSON, write it and return the path.
symbols.io_read_csv: Read a file and return parsed CSV rows.
symbols.io_write_csv: Serialize CSV rows, write them and return the path.
symbols.io_read_config: Return trimmed key/value strings from `key=value` lines; skip blanks, # comments and lines without a nonempty key; later keys replace earlier keys.
symbols.random_next_int: Advance `rng.state` using multiplier 48271 modulo 2147483647; return the new positive integer state.
symbols.random_float: Advance the generator and return a value strictly between zero and one.
symbols.random_int: Advance the generator and return an integer in inclusive `[lo, hi]`; reject reversed bounds.
symbols.random_choice: Return a randomly chosen input element; empty input returns `nil` without drawing.
symbols.random_shuffle: Return a shallow shuffled list copy using Fisher–Yates, advancing `rng`.
symbols.random_sample: Shuffle and return `count` entries without replacement; require `0 <= count <= len(xs)`.
symbols.random_normal: Return a Box–Muller normal draw centered at `mean` with multiplier `stddev`; advance the generator twice.
symbols.check: Increment passed/failed counters and print `FAIL: label` for false conditions; continue running the suite.
symbols.assert_equal: Record equality; include actual/expected display values in a failure label.
symbols.assert_not_equal: Record inequality against the unexpected value.
symbols.assert_near: Record whether absolute numeric difference is at most tolerance.
symbols.test_summary: Print totals and raise `fail` if any recorded assertion failed.
symbols.__passed: Mutable module-wide count of successful recorded assertions, initially zero.
symbols.__failed: Mutable module-wide count of failed recorded assertions, initially zero.
symbols.truthy: Convert a dynamic value to Boolean using runtime truthiness.
symbols.default: Return the fallback only when the value is `nil`.
symbols.Ok: Return a success map `{ok: true, value, error: nil}`.
symbols.Err: Return a failure map `{ok: false, value: nil, error}`.
symbols.Some: Return the same success-map representation as `Ok`.
symbols.None: Return `nil`; invoke as a zero-argument function.
symbols.__op_add: Internal map/record `+` hook dispatch; call the left operand's method with `(self, other)` or return `nil` when unavailable.
symbols.__op_sub: Internal map/record `-` hook dispatch; call the left operand's method with `(self, other)` or return `nil` when unavailable.
symbols.__op_mul: Internal map/record `*` hook dispatch; call the left operand's method with `(self, other)` or return `nil` when unavailable.
symbols.__op_div: Internal map/record `/` hook dispatch; call the left operand's method with `(self, other)` or return `nil` when unavailable.
symbols.native.may:__native_utf8_width: Native prelude helper: return the byte width of a valid UTF-8 leading byte.
symbols.native.may:__native_string_bytes: Native prelude helper: copy an in-range UTF-8 byte slice into a fresh string; the caller must preserve codepoint boundaries.
symbols.native.may:__native_ascii_case: Native prelude helper: copy a string, shifting the 26 ASCII letters starting at `low` by `delta`; other bytes are unchanged.
symbols.native.may:__native_find: Native prelude helper: return the byte offset of the first `sub` in `s` at or after byte `offset`, or -1.
symbols.is_space_code: True for ASCII space, tab, LF and CR character codes.
symbols.is_upper_code: True for ASCII uppercase letter codes 65..90.
symbols.is_lower_code: True for ASCII lowercase letter codes 97..122.
symbols.to_lower: Return an ASCII-lowercased string; other character codes pass through.
symbols.to_upper: Return an ASCII-uppercased string; other character codes pass through.
symbols.index_of: Return the first substring index or `-1`; an empty needle returns zero.
symbols.starts_with: True when the string begins with the supplied prefix.
symbols.ends_with: True when the string ends with the supplied suffix.
symbols.replace: Replace non-overlapping occurrences; an empty needle returns the original string.
symbols.chars: Return Unicode codepoints as one-character strings.
symbols.make_error: Construct a structured error object with category and message for the native runtime.
symbols.raise_error: Construct and raise a structured runtime error; does not return normally.
symbols.fail_list: Build and raise a fail-category error from displayable message items.
symbols.type_name: Return the tagged runtime type name.
symbols.raise_binop_error: Raise an operator/type error describing both operands and the operator.
symbols.raise_add_error: Raise the native addition operand-type error.
symbols.raise_exp_error: Raise the native exponentiation operand-type error.
symbols.raise_io_error: Raise an I/O-category error with the supplied message.
symbols.ptr: Return the integer address unchanged; pointer lifetime/validity remains the caller's responsibility.
symbols.print_error: Print a structured error's category/message and available stack text.
symbols.concat_lists: Return a shallow concatenation of two lists.
symbols.string_repr: Produce the native display representation for dynamic values.
symbols.type: Return the native runtime type name.
symbols.sign: Return -1, 0 or 1 according to comparison with zero.
symbols.parse_int: Parse a trimmed integer string with range checking; propagate conversion faults.
symbols.parse_float: Parse a trimmed floating-point string through native conversion.
symbols.pi: Return the binary64 approximation of π, 3.141592653589793.
symbols.e: Return the binary64 approximation of Euler's number, 2.718281828459045.
symbols.round: Round to the nearest integral Float; halfway values round toward positive infinity (`round(-2.5)` is `-2.0`).
symbols.tanh: Compute `(exp(2*x) - 1) / (exp(2*x) + 1)`; large inputs may overflow the exponential.
symbols.hypot: Return `sqrt(x*x + y*y)` without an overflow-resistant scaling algorithm.
symbols.cbrt: Return a sign-preserving cube root computed with fractional powers.
symbols.jd_is_space: Internal JSON whitespace predicate for space, tab, LF and CR.
symbols.jd_skip: Internal JSON parser: skip whitespace from index `i` and return the next index.
symbols.jd_hex: Internal JSON parser: decode one hexadecimal character or raise a parse fault.
symbols.jd_string: Internal JSON parser: decode a quoted string and return the parsed value and next position.
symbols.jd_number: Internal JSON parser: read a number and return the parsed value and next position.
symbols.jd_array: Internal JSON parser: read an array and return the parsed list and next position.
symbols.jd_object: Internal JSON parser: read an object and return the parsed map and next position.
symbols.jd_value: Internal JSON parser: dispatch by the next token and return the value and next position.
symbols.jq_escape: Internal JSON serializer: quote/escape a string including control characters.
symbols.chr: Return a one-character string from a character code.
symbols.ord: Return the first character's codepoint; require a nonempty string.
symbols.product: Multiply a numeric list, starting at one.
symbols.count: Return the count of values equal to the supplied value.
symbols.find: Return the first element satisfying the unary predicate, or `nil`.
symbols.zip: Return paired elements, stopping at the shorter list.
symbols.flatten: Return a one-level concatenation of nested lists.
symbols.unique: Return distinct list values in first-occurrence order.
symbols.range_step: Return an exclusive-end arithmetic progression in either direction; step zero returns an empty list.
symbols.pad_left: Prepend whole padding strings until the code-point width is reached; empty padding faults when more text is needed.
symbols.pad_right: Append whole padding strings until the code-point width is reached; empty padding faults when more text is needed.
symbols.split_lines: Split on LF, preserving empty fields.
symbols.get: Return the lookup value when non-nil, otherwise fallback; a present nil-valued entry also uses the fallback.
symbols.each: Call unary `f(x)` for every input element; return `nil`.
symbols.assert_eq: Raise an assertion error if actual and expected values differ.
symbols.ml_distance: Return Euclidean distance between equal-width numeric feature vectors.
symbols.ml_knn_predict: Return the majority label among k nearest training rows; require nonempty matching data and k within the training set size; votes use stringified label keys.
symbols.ml_kmeans: Return `{centers, labels, inertia}` after up to `iterations` assignment/update rounds; use random initial rows and retain centers for empty clusters.
symbols.ml_linear_fit: Train zero-initialized linear weights by batch gradient descent; return `{weights, bias}`.
symbols.ml_linear_predict: Return linear predictions for input rows using `{weights, bias}`.
symbols.ml_classical_sigmoid: Return sigmoid after clamping input to [-60, 60].
symbols.ml_logistic_fit: Train binary logistic regression by batch gradient descent; labels must be 0 or 1; return `{weights, bias}`.
symbols.ml_logistic_predict: Return probabilities for each feature row using the trained logistic model.
symbols.ml_one_hot: Return a row of floating 0/1 entries for each integer class label; validate labels and positive class count.
symbols.ml_train_test_split: Shuffle paired rows and return `{x_train, y_train, x_test, y_test}`; require at least two rows and fraction strictly between 0 and 1; ensure both partitions are nonempty.
symbols.ml_batches: Return consecutive `{x, y}` batches including a shorter final batch; require matching row counts and positive batch size.
symbols.ml_feature_stats: Return per-column population `{mean, scale}`; replace scales smaller than 1e-12 with 1.0; validate nonempty rectangular rows.
symbols.ml_standardize: Return `(x - mean) / scale` per column using previously fitted statistics.
symbols.ml_minmax_fit: Return per-column `{min, max}` statistics; require nonempty rows.
symbols.ml_minmax_transform: Return per-column [0,1] scaling using fitted bounds; constant columns become 0.0; values outside training bounds are not clipped.
symbols.FixedLayer: Typed layer descriptor with input/output widths and an offset into the shared parameter list.
symbols.FixedNetwork: Typed network containing layer descriptors, integer parameters and a positive integer scale.
symbols.nn_fixed_model: Validate dimensions, scale and output-major weights/biases; return a FixedNetwork. Scale is 1..32768, widths 1..1024 and absolute parameters at most 16*scale.
symbols.nn_fixed_predict: Return integer-scaled output values using softsign activation; validate input width and absolute input at most 16*scale; share network parameters without mutation.
symbols.ml_mse: Return MSE over nested prediction/target rows; validate matching nonempty batch counts; require matching nonempty rectangular widths as a caller precondition.
symbols.ml_mse_gradient: Return the elementwise MSE gradient normalized by total output count.
symbols.ml_binary_cross_entropy: Return output-count-averaged binary cross entropy, bounding each logarithm argument below by 1e-8.
symbols.ml_binary_cross_entropy_gradient: Return output-count-normalized (prediction-target) divided by max(1e-8, prediction*(1-prediction)).
symbols.ml_categorical_cross_entropy: Return batch-averaged categorical cross entropy from probability rows and target rows.
symbols.ml_categorical_cross_entropy_gradient: Return the categorical derivative `-target / clamped_probability / batch_count`.
symbols.ml_accuracy: Return classification accuracy; single outputs use a 0.5 threshold, multiple outputs use argmax; empty/mismatched batch counts return 0.0.
symbols.ml_confusion_matrix: Return a class-by-class count matrix indexed by actual then predicted class.
symbols.ml_classification_report: Return `{class, precision, recall, f1, support}` entries for each row of a confusion matrix; zero denominators yield zero.
symbols.ml_loss_value: Dispatch losses named `mse`, `binary_cross_entropy` or `cross_entropy`; reject other names.
symbols.ml_loss_gradient: Dispatch the matching gradient for the three supported loss names.
symbols.ml_train_batch: Run forward, loss, backward and an optimizer update in order; mutate model/optimizer and return loss.
symbols.ml_fit: Shuffle and train minibatches each epoch; mutate model, optimizer and RNG; return `{model, history}` with sample-weighted epoch losses.
symbols.ml_evaluate: Return `{loss, accuracy, predictions}` using the selected loss; prediction updates the model's forward caches.
symbols.ml_save: Write the model state dictionary as JSON; return the underlying write_file result. Does not save optimizer state.
symbols.ml_load: Read JSON layer states into an already constructed compatible model; return that model.
symbols.nn_model: Return an empty dynamic model `{layers: [], input_dim: 0, output_dim: 0}`.
symbols.nn_add_dense: Append a dense layer with random initialization and zero biases; validate positive compatible dimensions; mutate and return model.
symbols.nn_sigmoid: Return sigmoid after clamping its input to [-60,60].
symbols.nn_activate_scalar: Apply `linear`, `relu`, `sigmoid` or `tanh`; reject unknown scalar activation names.
symbols.nn_activate_row: Apply scalar activation to a row or use stabilized `softmax` for a full row.
symbols.nn_forward: Return output rows while storing each layer's input and output caches for backpropagation.
symbols.nn_activation_delta: Return the activation-adjusted gradient for one cached batch/output element, including the softmax Jacobian.
symbols.nn_backward: Populate gradient weights/biases from the last forward caches; propagate the gradient backward and return model.
symbols.nn_predict: Run `nn_forward` for input rows; update training caches.
symbols.nn_tensor_rows: Convert a rank-two tensor to nested rows; reject other ranks.
symbols.nn_predict_tensor: Return a tensor matrix of predictions, updating forward caches.
symbols.nn_forward_tensor: Convert a matrix tensor to rows, run forward and return matrix tensor outputs.
symbols.nn_backward_tensor: Convert matrix tensor gradients to rows and run backward; return model.
symbols.nn_parameter_count: Return the sum of dense weights and biases across all layers.
symbols.nn_state_dict: Return layer states containing weights, bias, activation and dimensions for JSON snapshots.
symbols.nn_load_state: Validate layer counts/dimensions and assign state weights/biases into the existing model; return model.
symbols.ml_sgd: Construct an SGD optimizer with positive learning rate and zero momentum.
symbols.ml_sgd_momentum: Construct SGD state with positive learning rate and momentum in [0,1).
symbols.ml_adam: Construct Adam state; require positive learning rate/epsilon and betas in [0,1).
symbols.ml_adam_default: Construct Adam using beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999 and epsilon=1e-8.
symbols.ml_zero_matrix_like: Return a same-shaped nested matrix of 0.0 entries.
symbols.ml_adam_matrix: Return updated `{param, first, second}` matrices using bias-corrected Adam moments and the current optimizer powers.
symbols.ml_adam_vector: Return updated `{param, first, second}` vectors using bias-corrected Adam moments.
symbols.ml_optimizer_step: Update dense model parameters and optimizer velocity/moments in place; return model. Run backward first.
symbols.tensor_size: Return the product of dimensions; an empty shape has scalar size one.
symbols.tensor: Return `{data, shape}` after checking nonnegative integer dimensions and matching element count; retain the data list reference and copy the shape list.
symbols.tensor_scalar: Wrap a scalar as a tensor with one element and empty shape.
symbols.tensor_vector: Return a shallow-copied rank-one tensor from a list.
symbols.tensor_matrix: Validate rectangular rows and flatten into a rank-two tensor; empty rows produce shape [0,0].
symbols.tensor_zeros: Return a tensor of floating zeros with the requested shape.
symbols.tensor_ones: Return a tensor of floating ones with the requested shape.
symbols.tensor_full: Return a tensor filled with the supplied value.
symbols.tensor_arange: Return a rank-one exclusive-stop arithmetic sequence; step cannot be zero; support positive and negative steps.
symbols.tensor_eye: Return an n-by-n floating identity matrix tensor.
symbols.tensor_rank: Return the number of shape dimensions.
symbols.tensor_reshape: Return a new tensor wrapper sharing data after validating the new shape's element count.
symbols.tensor_at: Return an element by flat index using list indexing rules.
symbols.tensor_at2: Return the element at row/column in a rank-two tensor; validate rank and coordinates.
symbols.tensor_map: Return a tensor of mapped data with the same shape.
symbols.tensor_same_shape: Compare two shape lists and return Bool; different ranks/dimensions return false without raising.
symbols.tensor_broadcast_shape: Return the compatible trailing-dimension broadcast shape; dimensions must match or be one.
symbols.tensor_broadcast_to: Return a tensor expanded to the requested compatible shape using row-major coordinate mapping.
symbols.tensor_broadcast_zip: Broadcast two tensors to a common shape and combine entries with a binary callback.
symbols.tensor_add_broadcast: Return elementwise addition after trailing-dimension broadcasting.
symbols.tensor_sub_broadcast: Return elementwise subtraction after trailing-dimension broadcasting.
symbols.tensor_mul_broadcast: Return elementwise multiplication after trailing-dimension broadcasting.
symbols.tensor_div_broadcast: Return elementwise division after trailing-dimension broadcasting; numeric division faults propagate.
symbols.tensor_zip: Combine equally shaped tensors with a binary callback; reject shape mismatches.
symbols.tensor_scale: Return each element multiplied by a scalar factor.
symbols.tensor_add_scalar: Return each element plus a scalar value.
symbols.tensor_sum: Return the sum of all tensor elements.
symbols.tensor_mean: Return the floating element mean, or nil for an empty tensor.
symbols.tensor_dot: Return the dot product of equal-length rank-one tensors.
symbols.tensor_transpose: Return the row-major transpose of a rank-two tensor.
symbols.tensor_sum_axis: Reduce a matrix on axis 0 or 1; negative axes normalize by rank; return a vector tensor.
symbols.tensor_mean_axis: Return axis sums divided by the reduced dimension; reject an empty reduced dimension.
symbols.tensor_softmax_rows: Return a rank-two tensor with stabilized softmax independently in each row.
symbols.tensor_concat_vectors: Concatenate two rank-one tensors into a vector tensor.
symbols.tensor_rows: Return a copied rank-two row interval [start,stop); validate the bounds.
symbols.tensor_matmul: Return a rank-two matrix product; require matching inner dimensions.
symbols.tensor_argmax: Return the first flat index of the largest element, or -1 for an empty tensor.
symbols.tensor_softmax: Return stabilized softmax for a rank-one tensor; empty input returns an empty vector.
symbols.Address: IPv4 host/port record; use address() for validation and canonicalization.
symbols.Socket: Owned descriptor, socket kind and operation timeout record; aliases share the descriptor and close state.
symbols.Datagram: UDP byte payload with its sender Address.
symbols.net_fault: Construct and raise a network error with operation and positive errno.
symbols.net_check: Return nonnegative syscall status or raise a network fault from the negated status.
symbols.net_timeout: Validate the allowed timeout range -1..2147483647 milliseconds.
symbols.net_deadline: Convert a timeout to a monotonic deadline, using -1.0 for unlimited waiting.
symbols.net_now: Return monotonic clock seconds using Linux clock_gettime.
symbols.net_remaining: Return remaining deadline milliseconds, rounded up, or -1 for unlimited waiting.
symbols.net_open: Validate a live descriptor and optional expected socket kind; return the descriptor.
symbols.net_buffer: Allocate a NUL-filled byte string; allow 0..16777216 bytes.
symbols.net_trim: Change a buffer's byte length and append a terminating NUL; require sufficient underlying allocation.
symbols.address: Validate/canonicalize the host and port and return Address; valid ports are 0..65535.
symbols.net_sockaddr: Encode a validated address as a Linux sockaddr_in byte buffer.
symbols.net_decode: Decode a Linux AF_INET sockaddr_in byte buffer into Address.
symbols.net_socket: Create a nonblocking, close-on-exec IPv4 descriptor; return Socket with a 30000 ms timeout.
symbols.net_discard: Close a socket during cleanup and mark it closed.
symbols.net_poll: Poll descriptor read/write readiness against a monotonic deadline, retrying interrupted calls.
symbols.socket_wait: Return readiness as Bool using the explicit timeout; false on timeout; do not change the socket timeout.
symbols.net_ready: Wait for readiness or raise a timeout fault for the named operation.
symbols.socket_local_address: Return the bound/local Address, including an OS-assigned ephemeral port.
symbols.tcp_connect_timeout: Connect to an IPv4 peer with an explicit timeout; reject port zero; clean up on failure and return Socket on success.
symbols.tcp_accept: Accept and return a connected Socket inheriting the listener's timeout.
symbols.net_receive: Read bytes into a supplied buffer interval against the same deadline; return the syscall byte count.
symbols.udp_send_to: Send a complete datagram and return the byte count; require nonzero destination port and payload at most 65507 bytes.
symbols.repeat: Return a string repeated n times; nonpositive counts produce an empty string.
symbols.substring: Return a string starting at codepoint index start and containing count codepoints; require indices within the source string.
symbols.range: Return an eager list of integers from inclusive a to exclusive b; the full-runtime source function takes exactly two arguments.
symbols.split: Split by a literal delimiter, preserving empty fields; an empty delimiter returns a one-element list containing the original string.
symbols.core:arena_new: Allocate one process-lifetime scratch arena with capacity rounded up to eight bytes; negative or oversized capacities terminate with status 70.
symbols.core:arena_alloc: Reserve an eight-byte-aligned scratch span; negative requests or capacity exhaustion terminate with status 70.
symbols.core:arena_reset: Reset the cursor without clearing bytes or returning pages; invalidate every previously returned span. Callers must discard all aliases before resetting.
symbols.core:arena_used: Read consumed scratch bytes including alignment padding.
symbols.core:arena_capacity: Read rounded scratch capacity in bytes.
symbols.core:core_heap_retained: Read total requested native chunk bytes, including ordinary allocations and arenas.
symbols.core:float_str: Format a boxed float with the shortest digits that parse back to the same value; spell nonfinite values nan, inf and -inf and keep the sign of negative zero.
symbols.native.may:float_str: Format a boxed float with the shortest digits that parse back to the same value; spell nonfinite values nan, inf and -inf and keep the sign of negative zero.
symbols.core:alloc: Allocate raw process-lifetime bytes; return a Ptr. Core heap exhaustion terminates with status 70.
symbols.core:memcpy: Copy raw bytes between valid, nonoverlapping caller-owned pointer spans.
symbols.core:gcd: Return the nonnegative greatest common divisor of two integers.
symbols.core:lcm: Return the nonnegative least common multiple, or zero if either input is zero; overflow terminates with status 70.
symbols.core:clamp: Bound an integer between low and high; callers provide low <= high.
symbols.core:sum: Sum integer elements with checked arithmetic.
symbols.core:is_space_code: Test ASCII space, tab, line feed or carriage return character codes.

native.may: This page also inventories runtime support functions (`__op_*`, `jd_*`, formatting and error helpers); their exposed names are not a separate stability guarantee.
Actual source arity wins over legacy catalogs: full-runtime `range(a, b)` takes two arguments, and `None()` is a call.
String case conversion is ASCII-only. String lengths and indices count codepoints; networking byte helpers operate on raw bytes.

Names asin, acos, atan, atan2 and powf are mentioned in older runtime comments, but are not registered callable APIs in the active mayc implementation; do not infer their availability from those comments.
string.may: `words` splits ASCII space, tab, carriage return and newline, dropping empty fields.
Padding requires a nonempty pad when growth is needed; multicharacter pads can overshoot width.
`csv` is a simple comma split; use `csv_parse` from the csv module for quoted CSV.
algo.may: `chunk` validates a positive size, including for empty input; invalid sizes raise `chunk size must be positive`.
Quicksort and merge_sort return the original list on length zero/one; larger results are newly assembled.
Grouping and deduplication use dynamic maps; group_by/count_by stringify keys.
collections.may: Stacks and queues store shared list references in maps; mutations are visible through aliases.
Queue pop advances a head index; consumed elements are retained in the backing list.
stack_peek on an empty stack uses out-of-range indexing and can fault; guard with stack_empty.
Sets use map keys and true values; set_remove returns a new map rather than mutating the original.
math.may: Integer division truncates toward zero; average and even-length median on integer inputs may therefore truncate. Use floating inputs or stats_mean/stats_median for fractional results.
factorial/fibonacci do not reject negative arguments; their empty loops return 1 and 0 respectively.
random.may: All draws mutate the explicit RNG state. This generator is intended for repeatable tests/simulations; it is not a cryptographic generator.
path.may: Operations are lexical; they do not resolve symlinks or access the filesystem. path_relative requires matching roots and returns `.` for identical paths.
functional.may: Memoization keys use str(arg); distinct arguments with identical display strings share a cached result.
test.may: Assertions record failures and keep running. Call test_summary to fail the program when any assertion failed. Counters are shared module state.
net.may: Requires the full Linux x86-64 native runtime; core/raw builds do not support this module.
No DNS, IPv6, TLS or HTTP. Use dotted IPv4 or localhost; ports are 0..65535, but peer port zero is invalid.
Default timeout is 30000 ms; -1 means unlimited, 0 means immediate, maximum finite value is 2147483647.
Sockets share descriptor ownership through aliases. Close explicitly or use with_socket; no automatic finalizer.
Binary payloads may contain NUL and invalid UTF-8. TCP receive allocation is at most 16 MiB; UDP payload is at most 65507 bytes.
Errors have kind network, message, operation and positive Linux errno. Timeout=110, invalid input=22, closed socket=9, oversize UDP=90, early exact-read EOF=0.
core: See [arena ownership and allocation growth](../../internals/CORE_MEMORY.md). Core has no collector; ordinary strings/lists and the arena itself retain process-lifetime storage.

native.may:get: The implementation treats a nil lookup as absent, so a present nil value returns the fallback.
native.may:extern_c: The wrapper has six positional parameters and returns a raw integer C result; use ccall for a list of up to six integer arguments.
native.may:range_step: Step zero returns an empty list; the stop is exclusive in either direction.
native.may:json_parse: Returns dynamic maps/lists/scalars; rejects trailing content and malformed strings. See the implementation for supported Unicode escape behavior.
native.may:round: Float return; halfway values, including negative ones, round toward positive infinity. Convert with int() where an Int is needed.
net.may:tcp_receive: Require 1..16777216 maximum bytes. An empty result means orderly TCP EOF.
net.may:tcp_receive_exact: Require 0..16777216 bytes; zero returns an empty string without a read; premature EOF raises.
net.may:udp_receive_from: Require 1..65535 maximum bytes; an oversized packet is consumed and raises errno 90. Empty datagrams are valid.
native.may:json_stringify: Object keys are sorted before serialization and must be strings. Cyclic collections are not valid JSON trees; do not pass self-referential values.

mkdir: Create a directory with Linux mode 0755; raise an I/O error on failure.
exec: Start a child using fork/execve and return its PID; argv is a nonempty list of argument strings.
wait: Wait for a child and return its decoded exit status; failures raise; signal termination is encoded as 128 plus signal number.
system: Run /bin/sh -c and wait for its exit status.
type: Return a tagged runtime type name: Int, Float, Str, Bool, Nil, List or Map.
trunc: Truncate a numeric value toward zero; NaN, infinities and results outside the Int range raise an arithmetic fault.
ln: Natural logarithm; use positive numeric inputs.
log2: Base-two logarithm; use positive numeric inputs.
log10: Base-ten logarithm; use positive numeric inputs.
pow: Floating power; the ** operator also supports native integer dispatch.
cmp: Return a negative, zero or positive comparison result.
char_at: Read a string codepoint as an integer; require a valid codepoint index.
char_from: Encode a character code as a one-character string.
to_map: Create a runtime map from a list of key/value pairs.
str_of: Internal native display conversion used by str.
int_to_str: Convert an integer to its decimal display string.
str_cmp: Compare strings, returning a signed ordering result.
value_eq: Native value equality used by assertions and dynamic comparisons.
value_tag: Inspect runtime tags: Int=0, Str=1, Nil=2, false=3, true=4, List=5, Float=6, Map=7; implementation support API.
map_keys: Return runtime map keys; native keys delegates here.
map_values: Return runtime map values; native values delegates here.
rt_raise: Internal structured-error raise used by native and network helpers; unwinds to a may handler.
